ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

LABA monotherapy

An adult with asthma requests a long-acting beta agonist inhaler alone because it controls symptoms for many hours. Which prescribing principle is most important when considering a LABA for asthma treatment?

  1. Use it with an inhaled corticosteroid-containing regimen
  2. LABA alone is preferred because inflammation never matters
  3. A LABA replaces every need for corticosteroids
  4. All LABAs are antibiotics
  5. LABAs permanently cure asthma after one dose
Answer and explanation

Use it with an inhaled corticosteroid-containing regimen

LABA monotherapy is not appropriate in asthma; anti-inflammatory treatment is required.

Option explanations

Use it with an inhaled corticosteroid-containing regimen: LABA monotherapy is not appropriate in asthma; anti-inflammatory treatment is required.

LABA alone is preferred because inflammation never matters: Asthma includes airway inflammation.

A LABA replaces every need for corticosteroids: Bronchodilation does not replace anti-inflammatory control.

All LABAs are antibiotics: They are bronchodilators.

LABAs permanently cure asthma after one dose: They provide pharmacologic control, not a permanent cure.
